method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs and street-name labels
why_not_one_block_off: Sheet 52 covers avenues N-O 1/2 and sheet 53 covers O 1/2-Q, so Avenue O 1/2 is the only shared avenue; both sheets letter 'AVENUE O 1/2' in it and both print its width '70' inside the corridor. Sheet 52's east frontage on it is even -- 2502 2504 2506 ... 2528 -- and sheet 53's west frontage is odd -- 2501 2503 2505 ... 2527 -- i.e. the two sides of one avenue. The cross-street numbering turns across it: sheet 52 ends at 1722 1724 while sheet 53 begins 1801 1803, the 1700/1800 hundred-block change. Sheet 52's block face reads x=3079 and sheet 53's x=268; with the printed 70 ft = 206 px (measured on Ave O 2085/2291, Ave P 1058/1268, Ave P 1/2 2059/2264) the centre lies 103 px inside each face. Sheet 53's value also matches grid extrapolation from Ave P (164.5).
